1: He who, made of the widely flashing wheel of diverse states, comes to be the objects of experience — whose one, given to contemplation, is thus the bond of nondifference: He, Śaṃbhura, woe-averting, triumphs — treasury of the lights of knowing.
2: By the sage Dvaipāyana this scripture was expounded, measured by hundreds of thousands; here liberation is established as the fruit — and mādhānya than [L0-fork] — its other dharma-and-rest is recited to nourish it.
3: Liberation, by name, complete-differentiation in form, all-knowing, auspicious-natured in all instruments and more — free from need, in Bhagavān the Lord, ever-risen: dissolution — this much, toward it [prathiḥ L0-fork], in summary.
4: Although liberation by name is celebrated in other connections, yet the Bhagavadgītā is the giver of true attainment.
5: In them, although earlier ones made many expositions, yet my attempt too is reasonable — revealing its hidden meaning.
6: From the oral tradition of Bhaṭṭa Indurāja, examined long with thought, made by Abhinavagupta — this here is the Gītārthasaṃgraha.
